title: 08.03.2026 update
overview:
This battle adjustment was done with the aim of shifting the game's balance by looking at every character and making adjustments.

While we believe the game's balance has reached a reasonably stable state thanks to repeated adjustments, the relative strength of each character has not shifted significantly in recent updates. Due to this, we decided to implement changes specifically to shake things up.

Please note that there are no adjustments applied universally to all characters.

Modern Control Adjustments
With this battle adjustments we've updated certain normal moves (ones that utilize the attack button) and special moves (ones that utilize the SP button) for specific characters. Additionally, for moves that are performed by pressing Down+SP, you can now select the strength of the special move by inputting SP with Down-back, Down or Down-Forward.

This adjustment requires players to relearn specific moves and adds a layer of complexity to the controls, but were done with the aim of improving usability and providing Modern control players with a larger range of options while in the neutral. Please note that Assisted Combos have also been updated for some characters to reflect these changes. Please refer to the character-specific sections for full details.

general.change: Fixed an issue where holding back during the screen-freeze of an opponent's Drive Reversal would cancel out a previous command or button inputs.

Luke.concept:
In addition to previous adjustments that saw Luke's forward moving attacks easier to use, Luke has also gained more follow-up options and situations, more damage for his special moves when used as combo enders, making it easier for him to net damage.

Standing Medium Punch, Snapback Combo (Medium Punch > Medium Punch > Medium Punch > Medium Punch)
Along with reducing the attack's hurtbox so it can win out against opposing strikes, we've increased the returns for Snap Back Combo on Punish Counter as Luke can now follow-up with Super Art 1 outside of the corner, and with Rising Uppercut while in the corner. This makes it easier to use the attack as your first poke option in neutral, improving its utility in a match.

Standing Heavy Punch
The adjustment to the situation on block reduces the risk of using the move as a standalone option, and makes it easier to create sequences like Standing Heavy Punch into Medium Sand Blast, where your opponent has to keep on the defensive, making this a stronger option for such strings.

Jumping Medium Punch
This attack features improved air-to air interactions thanks to faster start-up, and can now be used as a follow-up attack after Light Flash Knuckle (Hold) and Overdrive Flash Knuckle. A previous adjustment provided Luke with the ability to combo Light Attack > Light Flash Knuckle > Light Rising Uppercut, but this adjustment will now give more value to Overdrive Flash Knuckle as part of a combo, as it was previously overshadowed by stronger options.

Sand Blast (↓↘→+Punch)
This move now knocks down on anything bigger than a counter hit, which is a significant change. While Luke will see a smaller return with some combos when in the corner, in the middle of the stage you can now follow-up with Drive Rush, etc. after a counter hit to apply pressure. Now Luke can capitalize on this projectile's high speed when he's using it as a zoning tool.

Jamie.concept:
We have enhanced the performance of the Standing Heavy Kick—which offers significant reward on hit—and the Standing Light Punch (at Drunkenness Level 1 or higher), a key move for neutral play and combos.

Additionally, we have adjusted various special moves, including target combos and Freeflow Strikes (↓↘→+Punch > →+Punch > →+Punch),
and have boosted the character's overall strength to ensure their unique characteristics stand out more prominently as their Drunkenness Level increases.

We've improved Jamie's Standing Heavy Kick, as it's a key move for him to net big returns, and his Standing Light Punch (Drink Level 1 or higher), an important attack in the neutral. Adjustments were also made to his target combos and various special moves such as Free Flow Strikes (↓↘→+Punch > →+Punch > →+Punch) to increase his overall strength and ensure his unique characteristics stand out more as he increases his Drink Level.

Standing Heavy Kick
The kick's range is extended during its active frames, making it easier to use as long-range poke with a good return. The pushback on hit and block adjustment along with the extended attack hitbox on the tip of the attack allows him to cancel into a special move for a guaranteed sequence, and avoids situations where the attack would not reach and combos would be dropped or he'd eat a counter attack.

Free Flow Strikes (Regular/Overdrive) (↓↘→+Punch or 2 Punches > →+Punch > →+Punch)
With the regular version of the attack, we gave more advantages to choosing the Punch route over the Kick route that nets you a drink by increasing the blowback time on hit, allowing Jamie to create better situations for himself.

With the Overdrive version, the disadvantage on block after blocking the 1st follow-up attack is updated so a guaranteed counter is no longer possible. This lets Jamie use the attack at close range for combos or situations where he wants to turn the tables on someone.

In addition, both versions also benefit from a shared adjustment when hitting a mid-air opponent, making it easier to connect with the follow-up attacks.

Manon.concept:
By improving her mid-range attacks, increased active frames on her Manège Doré command throw, and making Overdrive Dégagé a new tool for combo routes, Manon has undergone adjustments aimed at expanding her neutral and combo options.

Standing Medium Kick
The attack hitbox on the second active frame that was expanded forward previously, now matches the size of the hitbox on the 1st active frame. This adjustment is aimed at making the attack different from other mid-range pokes, and is designed to extend its reach and make the attack less likely to lose against the opponent's preemptive attack. On top of that, the opponent now goes into a longer knockback when the attack lands, and can now combo into Light Renversé on counter hit. This gives Manon a bigger return when she beats out an opponent's attack.

Tomoe Derrière (↘+Heavy Kick)
Changes were made to the blowback on Punish Counter, giving Manon a bigger advantage on wake-up. It also now combos into Crouching Heavy Kick, Super Art 1 or Super Art 2.

Overdrive Dégagé
(↓↙←+Two Kicks)
By changing the hit effect on an mid-air opponent, it's now easier to use this attack in a combo route or connect from Révérence (←+Heavy Punch) when it lands on a mid-air opponent. You can also combo into Light Renversé on a mid-air hit, giving you yet another way to up your Medal level. In conjunction with these adjustments, we've also tweaked the combo count limits for other special moves.

Kimberly.concept:
The biggest change we've made to Kimberly is increasing her Shuriken Bomb Stock limit from two to three. We updated the input command and general function of Genius at Play accordingly, so give her a try and see how she plays!

We also improved the main parts of her checking toolkit by powering up her Standing Medium Kick and giving her more spacing options with Hidden Variable (↓↙← + Punch), giving her more ways to attack from mid-range.

Standing Medium Kick
We made the attack more reliable from mid-range by removing the hurtbox that appeared on the attacking foot before start-up.

Initially, we believed that adding a hurtbox to the attack's startup would prevent players relying on it to heavily, given its long reach and ability to cancel. However, given her previous battle adjustments—like the strengthening of her pokes, combo-starter scaling, and hurtbox adjustments—we found this precaution to be a bit of an over-correction, so we've walked it back.

Hidden Variable (↓↙← + Punch)
Now, instead of appearing directly in front of the opponent when the Punch button is held, Kimberly will appear wherever she activated the move from and slide forward from there.

Previously, the normal and Overdrive version of this move were easier to read and respond to, so by introducing the ability to change where kimberly appears, we hope it'll make it less risky for her to use either version.

Normal/Overdrive Genius at Play
Like before, Kimberly starts the fight with two Shuriken Bomb stock, but now she can use Genius at Play to gain a third.

Previously, Genius at Play could only be used when Kimberly had no Shuriken Bomb stock. We've changed this so that Kimberly will gain Shuriken Bomb stock so long as she has two or less. We also adjusted the input command from ↓↓ + Punch to ↓↓ + Kick.

Modern Controls

Emergency Stop/Torso Cleaver input command update
Torso Cleaver and Emergency Stop's command input have swapped, with Torso Cleaver now performed with ←+Attack, and Emergency Stop is now performed with Neutral+Attack

The intent behind this adjustment is to prevent accidental inputs. One way Kimberly can start her powerful offense is from anti-air crouching heavy punch followed by Sprint into Emergency Stop to pressure opponents when they land. However there were instances where requiring either a forward or back input for the Emergency Stop caused the input to reverse, and some moves were being performed unintentionally.

Genius at Play/Shuriken Bomb/Shuriken Bomb Special
Now that Kimberly can perform this attack even if she has two or fewer stocks, the command input has undergone some significant changes. The added complexity, which now requires holding a direction or a button after the input can be seen on the battle adjustment list so please try them out in training mode.

Marisa.concept:
The primary focus for Marisa this time around is improving her ability to use her medium and heavy attacks, plus her special moves.
Overall, we aimed at improving the merits of using her slow, but hard-hitting attacks to make her more satisfying to use.

Standing Medium Punch, Medium Two-Hitter (Medium Punch > Medium Punch)
The properties when hitting a mid-air opponent now allows for Medium Two-Hitter to connect as a true combo even if the initial Medium Punch hits the opponent in mid-air. Previously, if the first Medium Punch connected on a mid-air opponent, the second attack would whiff, leaving the opponent open to a counterattack. With this change, it makes the attack much easier to use.

Standing Heavy Punch (Hold), Heavy Two-Hitter (Heavy Punch Hold > Heavy Punch)
The frame advantage on the held Standing Heavy Punch now allows for the Heavy One-Two to become a natural block string. The held version now offers better frame advantage and forward movement compared to the regular version, letting Marisa to maintain her scary offensive pressure. While opponents can counter Marisa if they anticipate her holding the Heavy Punch, forcing the opponent to block this will now create a very good advantage for her.

Falx Crusher (→+Heavy Kick)
Magna Bunker (←+Heavy Punch) now connects as a follow-up when Falx Crusher connects as a Punish Counter, giving Marisa a much better return for landing this attack if they use it to punish an opponent's attack. We've made this adjustment to make sure Marisa can get the best return on a punish counter hit, while taking into account the returns she gets on Standing Heavy Punch and Kick, which also gives her a high damage return.


Tonitrus (↓↙←+Kick > Punch > Punch)
To give players an opportunity to check an opponent's reaction and the situation before committing to the follow-up hit, we've delayed the timing for the transition into the attack after the first attack is block, while still allowing it to be a natural block string.

Lily.concept:
Lily's most significant update is the ability to add a follow-up strike to Light Condor Wind. Previously, after long-reaching attacks like crouching heavy punch or Horn Breaker (← + Heavy Punch) is blocked, Lily couldn't create low risk blockstrings unless she used Drive or a Windclad stock for cancel. Because of this, invincible reversals would often interrupt her flow, and made it difficult for her to establish an offensive. Her new follow-up strike can still be punished if done too close to the opponent, just like the follow-up from other versions, but when it's blocked at max or near max range, it's much more difficult to punish. The startup is also as fast as the Overdrive version, letting Lily create real pressure. As one strategy, Lily can walk forward and use a heavy normal canceled into Light Condor Wind and force opponents to block to whittle down their Drive gauge.

However, there are two things to keep in mind with this change
1. The command to store Windclad stock without attacking has changed.
2. The strike-follow-up of the Light version doesn't give Lily a Windclad stock.

When holding Light Condor Wind, you can now cancel the technique by pressing any Kick button in Classic and any button except Light or Assist while in Modern, in addition to releasing the Light attack button.

By holding one of those buttons immediately after performing the held version of Light Condor Wind, Lily can immediately cancel out of the technique while still adding a Windclad stock, which will reproduce the same effect the non-hold version had up until now. We understand these control changes may take some time to get accustomed to, but we believe this will significantly expand Lily's options and help address some of the difficulties she's previously faced. We encourage Lily players to spend some time to learn these new mechanics and take full advantage of them

JP.concept:
We felt that the risk-reward balance of some of JP's moves had become too skewed and that players had few ways to answer them, so we've adjusted them accordingly.

We also made adjustments to rectify issues that were introduced by the previous patch. For example, in making it possible to use Departure: Shadow from non-cancelable moves, players could instead use Departure: Window, making it impossible to counter with just a perfect parry or invincible attacks.

Finally, we've made adjustments to Departure that will hopefully expand on its utility and attack sequencing.

Standing Heavy Punch, Stribog (Light, Medium, Overdrive) (↓↘→+Light Punch or Medium Punch or Two Punches)
Both standing heavy punch and Stribog have had their standby block hitboxes changed, which should make them more effective as mid to long-range pokes.

Standing Heavy Punch is a move with long reach and a hurtbox that does not extend far forward, so it was difficult for opponents to hit the startup of this move, making the risk of challenging it very high depending on the character. Considering that it causes a knockdown against airborne opponents and it has a wealth of cancel options to keep it safe, delaying the standby block hitbox will make it a bit easier to back away and make it whiff, making it less effective at it's maximum distance.

JP can already discourage the opponent walking back with his far reaching crouching medium kick, and although this does not have as large of returns as his standing heavy punch, he can also control it with Stribog, which now has a faster standby block hitbox.

Bylina (→+Heavy Kick)
After connecting with the first hit, the hitbox of the second hit has been extended towards JP, so it the second hit should connect more easily. Since the move moves JP forward, the second hit would often whiff when it hit airborne opponents deep in the first hit, on during corner combos, so it should now be more consistent overall. However, the way the opponent is knocked back may have changed in your current combos, so make sure to check if you need to make some adjustments.

Overdrive Amnesia (↓↓+Two Kicks)
When the counter hurtbox connects with a throw move, the time JP is able to move afterwards is now later. Countering a normal throw will now leave JP at +4, so countering a throw while in the corner will no longer guarantee JP a back throw. Also, when a normal throw's third active frame overlaps with the first frame after your throw invincibility disappears when getting up, Overdrive Amnesia will counter the throw and leave him at +3, so a light attack is no longer guaranteed as a follow-up. It's now more difficult switch sides after a successful counter, and you'll have to be more selective with how you use the advantage from a successful counter.

Juri.concept:
Juri mostly has changes to her normal moves, including properties on grounded hits for increased returns, and less pushback on hit for light attacks to strengthen her strings. Although they aren't very flashy changes, we hope it will have a large impact on her play.

Crouching Medium Punch (normal and chain combo)
We extended the hitbox to make this more effective at anti-airing, but this had the unintended effect of beating out most other character's crouching punches when used as a poke. There were cases where even though Juri's hitbox seemed far from the opponent's attacking arm or leg it would still beat out their move, especially against attacks that hit higher up. We've remedied this by making her hitbox only active against airborne opponents.

Standing Heavy Kick (normal)
The hit effect on punish counter has changed, allowing for more varied follow-ups. Until now the moves that would connect with this were very limited, but now depending on the distance you can follow into things like Drive Rush crouching light punch into Super Art 3, so you can now adjust your combos depending on the situation.

Korenzan (normal) (←+Heavy Kick)
This can now combo into Ankensatsu on normal hit, giving it more benefits for hitting grounded opponents. It should now be more useful at close ranges for hit confirming.

Dee Jay.concept:
Dee Jay has had his pressure at close range strengthened from decreased pushback on his light attacks, and received some buffs to his lesser-used special moves. He is also now able to adjust the amount he moves from some of his feint attacks, making his offense that much more flustering.

Sunrise Heel (→+Medium Kick)
The behavior when hitting an in-air opponent has changed, giving him more advantage. Canceling into an Super Art should now always combo regardless of the height the move connects.

Light Jackknife Maximum (Charge ↓, then ↑+Light Kick)
Holding back after performing the move will now move you forward less. Now you can use it land on either side of the opponent at close ranges, or as a surprise attack at a distance.

Overdrive Machine Gun Uppercut (↓↙←+Two Punches)
The timing for when you can move after hitting has changed greatly, giving you much more advantage. Since this move has less opportunities to combo into than Overdrive Jus Cool, we adjusted it so that it gives good damage as well as leaves you in a good situation.

We tried to improve Cammy's ground game by expanding her zoning capabilities and powering up moves that help her close the distance to take advantage of her signature close-range fighting style. We also made some adjustments to improve her surprise attacks.

Ryu.concept:
Ryu has received adjustments aimed at improving his ability to maintain offensive momentum after successfully landing attacks. E. Honda.concept:
Honda's adjustments primarily focus on balancing his mid-range attacks. His standing medium punch had good reach and left him in a very good position after it hits, so we've slightly increased the risk on it if the attack misses, while giving more benefits to his other poking options.

Standing Heavy Kick
Thanks to adjustments on recovery when the first hit is blocked coupled with adjustments to Sumo Step and Teppo Triple Slaps, canceling the first hit of his standing heavy kick into regular or Overdrive Teppo will now create situations where the opponent is punished hard if they try to interrupt your attacks. The Overdrive version of Teppo is an especially powerful offensive tool, giving you frame advantage on block and good comboability when it lands as a counter hit, making it an even more valuable offensive tool.

Harai Kick (Forward + Heavy Kick)
When this attack lands on a standing opponent as a Punish Counter, they'll slide along the ground, giving you a huge frame advantage. This will let Honda do tricks like chasing the opponent with a Medium Sumo Headbutt to set up a wake-up pressure situation.

Sumo Dash (Normal) (↓↘→+Kick), Teppo Triple Slaps (Normal) (↓↘→+Kick > Punch > Punch)
The timing transition from Sumo Dash to Teppo Triple Slaps is sped up, allowing you to combo from medium attacks. In addition, the increased forward movement before the attack begins makes this easier for Honda to use this technique as a surprise attack or poking tool. Mixing this Sumo Headbutt and Sumo Smash will keep opponents on their toes while you maintain your pressure. The adjustments made to hit effects on mid-air opponents were done to minimize any effect on existing set up strategies.

Blanka.concept:
Blanka received changes to the properties on his mid-range normal and special moves, as well as the held version of Electric Thunder. In addition, Wild Edge and Wild Nail were being used outside of their intended purposes, so we've evened out the parts of them that stuck out too much, and also adjusted his other normal attacks to make them more useful.

Wild Edge (←+Medium KIck)
Considering the short reach against crouching opponents and area of the attack, this move was designed to be used at short reach or as an anti-air. However, since Blanka's hurtbox doesn't move forward during the move and it's able to cancel into Drive Rush and special moves, this move ended up being stronger than intended. Its high reach and difficulty to whiff punish made it strong enough that his other pokes lost meaning, so we've buffed Blanka's other mid-range pokes as well as made Wild Edge easier to whiff punish through longer whiff recovery and a larger hurtbox. This added recovery means it will also be more difficult to bait your opponent's Drive Reversal after a knockdown, so be careful when using it multiple times.

Wild Nail (→+Heavy Punch)
This move is intended to be a heavy attack with a special property on Punish Counter, but we had made it harder to be used to attack over the opponent's projectiles by adding a special projectile-only hurtbox right before the move becomes active. However, Wild Nail's special hurtbox was higher up than others so projectiles with a normal height like Hadoken had a hard time colliding with it. Therefore, we expanded this special hurtbox, so now most projectiles should properly stop the move before it becomes active. Projectiles that fly low to the ground should still have a hard time colliding with this hurtbox as intended.

Normal Electric Thunder (Held) (↓↙←+Punch (hold))
We've changed the properties of this move for the held version. The move will automatically transition into a follow-up on hit, and on block it will do multiple hits to chip at your opponent's Drive Gauge as well as leave you at advantage. This is easy to set up after a knockdown in the corner, so it should provide another option besides Wild Edge to give yourself an advantage on knockdown. The held version's hitbox has also been changed to a projectile, so it should now win out against almost every character's Super Art 1 as well as be a great way to chip at the opponent's health during burnout.

Guile.concept:
In this round of battle adjustments, we've improved a number of Guile's normal, unique, and special moves. For his combos, we've added some new elements to come up with some fresh combos, and with standing heavy kick's attack startup, the difficulty of some combos depending on opponent size, such as Sonic Boom > Standing Heavy Kick have been relaxed.

Standing Heavy Kick
We've adjusted this move so that it comes out faster, allowing Guile to use it in the neutral or as a poke easier. On the combo front, counter hit crouching medium punch > Cancel Drive Rush now allows for combo possibilities, so hitting with the tip of Burning Straight into Sonic Boom, etc. can now combo more consistently. On the other hand, if Standing Heavy Kick lands immediately after a Drive Rush, it leaves Guile closer to the opponent than before, so this may effect some existing combos, but we believe this is overall a big improvement for Guile.

Drake Fang (↓ + Medium Kick ‣ → + Medium Punch)
In neutral exchanges, using this move after Crouching Medium Kick disproportionately favored Guile, so we reduced the ground bound time that allowed Heavy Somersault Kick to connect. In exchange, we've strengthened the light version of Somersault Kick so it can be used as a follow-up attack.

Light Somersault Kick (Charge ↓, then ↑+Kick)
By adding a combo-only attack hitbox to the second frame of this move, we've made it easier to connect with quick attacks in the neutral game.
This adjustment boosts its utility as a combo tool by allowing it to connect in situations where follow-ups were previously out of range, such as after Drake Fang hits from a distance or when the tip of Crouching Medium Punch scores a counter hit but Double Shot (↓+Medium Punch > ↓+Medium Punch) would not reach.

Additionally, we expanded the collision hitbox that appears while Guile is in the air upward, making it easier to connect with an opponent directly in front him instead of passing right through unharmed.

Super Art 1: Sonic Hurricane (Charge ←, then →←→ + Any Punch)
We wanted to improve this move's ease of use in combos. As a result, we've made it possible to follow up with a light or medium Sonic Hurricane after a Heavy Sonic Hurricane, provided the initial hit connects on a grounded opponent.

Ken.concept:
Ken has fewer adjustments overall, but we improved a wide range of combos and attack sequences, so players will have some new tools to utilize in his neutral game.

Standing Medium Punch
By increasing the momentum left by Drive Rush, we've made it easier to force a mix-up between a low attack (like Crouching Light Kick into Standing Light Punch) and a normal throw after an opponent blocks it at close range. This also improves the reach of Crouching Heavy Punch, which deals decent damage when it connects, making this a powerful tool for initiating an offensive.

Crouching Medium Punch
By increasing the knockback time, we've made it possible for moves like Standing Light Kick (on normal hit) and Crouching Medium Kick (on Punish Counter) to combo reliably without relying on cancels, making the move more valuable in close-range attack sequences. While the damage of the move itself has been decreased, that change was made to accommodate for what we expect will be an overall damage output increase because of its adjusted follow-up capabilities.

Quick Dash (Two Kicks), Forward Step Kick (→ + Heavy Kick during Quick Dash)
Forward Step Kick now comes out quicker, making it possible to land hits with the tip of the attack from closer range or with better timing than before. While adjustments like reduced payoff on Punish Counters and decreased pushback on block may seem negative, we've tried to balance that by making sure the move has synergy with Ken's other zoning tools, like Standing Heavy Kick and Hadoken. This adjustment allows Ken's other moves to function more effectively, significantly giving him more tools to improve his mid-to-long-range game.

Finally, the move can now be mixed into combos whether Ken is standing or airborne, which makes it easier for him to respond to a wider variety of situations.

Chun-Li has received adjustments aimed at making both Hazanshu and Tensho Kicks easier to use, as well as improvements to Serenity Stream and its follow-up options. In particular, Hazanshu can now be selected by strength in Modern, and the light version has been made safer on block, reducing its risk and improving its effectiveness as a poking tool.

The combo count upper limit has also been adjusted so the medium version of Tensho Kicks will connect in situations where the heavy version of Tensho Kicks would also be used. This change is intended to give players a reason to choose between the medium and heavy version depending on the flow of the match and their desired follow-up.

Zangief.concept:
The change to Power Stomps adds another low attack option to Zangief's options. We've also looked to increase the situations players can aim to go for Double Lariat and Russian Suplex, and reduced the number of situations he's left at a disadvantage when whiffing an attack or trying to take back his turn.

Power Stomps (↓↓+Medium Kick > Medium Kick > Medium Kick)
The first hit can now be canceled into a special move, which along with the reduced hurtbox on the feet, makes it a viable option when trying to counter-poke an opponent's low attack. This can now work in conjunction with Standing Heavy Punch, which is already a vital tool in Zangief's arsenal thanks to its armor properties. Coupled with this main adjustment are changes such as adding combo-starter scaling and preventing follow-up attacks if the first hit whiffs.

Double Lariat (Normal) (Two Punches)
We have expanded the attack hitbox against crouching opponents, but this only occurs if the attack is performed as a cancel from a normal attack. This adjustment ensures that if the attack connects with the opponent's body, such as when landing the tip of crouching Medium Punch or a standing Light Kick on Punish Counter, Double Lariat it will always combo so long as you hold forward (→). The adjustment to Double Lariat's movement distance also ensures that the distance between characters after the attack finishes remains the same as before when holding forward.


Russian Suplex (Normal) (→↘↓↙←+Heavy Kick)
We've adjusted how this move works so that using Heavy Kick will always result in Russian Suplex no matter the distance. This adjustment is to prevent any confusion whether Russian Suplex or Siberian Express will be performed when at max throw range.

Although the damage for the Heavy version is slightly lower than the Light or Medium versions, the post-attack situation and Super Art gain is the same, in addition to its effective range being expanded, making it easier for players to choose between this attack or Screw Piledriver depending on the situation.

Rashid.concept:
Rashid mostly received changes to his longer reaching normal and special moves. His pokes and longer reaching moves are now easier to use, and his Overdrive Arabian Cyclone has received a new role in covering mid to long-ranges.

Crouching Heavy Punch
The standby block hitbox now happens earlier, so now it should be harder for the opponent to avoid the attack while sitting in its range. Now you can utilize its longer range as an effective mid-range poke.

Crescent Kick (→+Heavy Kick)
The knockback time on hit has been extended, so now you can follow with something like a crouching medium kick on Punish Counter. You'll now get more than just frame advantage when you, for example, get a Punish Counter by avoiding a sweep from a bit farther away. You can also link into a standing light punch on hit now, so make sure you properly discern the situation to get the most out of these changes.

Overdrive Arabian Cyclone (↓↙←+Two Punches)
The extended standby block timing on the first hit now makes it more difficult to back out of the second hit, and now whiffing the first hit but having the second guarded gives you advantage on block, giving it a new use. Alongside improvements to her normal attacks used for poking and whiff punishing, A.K.I. has also received adjustments to special moves that didn't see a lot of use, giving them new roles within her overall game plan and neutral strategy.

Qiong Qi (Standing Heavy Punch > Heavy Punch)

This change will now make it easier to apply pressure even after landing the move at long range. Additionally, if the first Standing Heavy Punch connects at close range or hits near the corner, you can follow-up with additional attacks.

Overdrive Nightshade Chaser (↓↙← + Two Punches > → + Heavy Punch)
The claw strike follow-up will now poison opponents even if it's blocked. This gives the attack a very distinct utility, and gives A.K.I. a significant tool for her pressure game and offensive strings. However, opponents will not be poisoned if only Nightshade Pulse is blocked, and the poison can also be avoided by parrying the attack, meaning players will still have to read the situation and be smart with its usage.

Light Cruel Fate (↓↙← + Light Kick)

Ed.concept:
Ed's ability to take advantage of openings with his long-reaching normals is already very strong, but he had a couple of tools that could let him turn the tide of the match to his favor even if he gets backed into the corner, meaning that the risk he carried while in the corner was much less than other characters.

Because Ed carrying less risk in the corner ran counter to our risk vs reward in the neutral, we adjusted the moves that provided the most dramatic single-interaction momentum swings for him. Specifically, we weakened his back throw situation, which was one of Ed's most common side-switch tools, as well as weakening the advantage he gained after a held Psycho Flicker was blocked, which was a common setup for his throw game.

However, we did improve Ed's ability to proactively go on the offensive by enhancing his situation after Flicker Combination (Light kick > Light Kick > Light Kick) and adjusting the projectile speed on Overdrive Psycho Shot based on strength, which will make it easier for him to create opportunities to move forward while applying pressure.

Rib Crusher (← + Light Punch + Light Kick)
Increased recovery after a hit means that Ed will be at a disadvantage if he performs a forward dash after this attack hits. Now, if you want to maintain your corner pressure after this hit, using attacks out of Drive Rush will be your primary option.

Overdrive Psycho Shoot (↓↘→ + Two Punches > → + Light or Heavy Punch)
The light version now travels more slowly, while the heavy version travels more quickly. The faster heavy version can create some strong pressure as an opponent's reactions will be tested more heavily. Against opponents who have a habit of using parry against the projectile, the slower light version will function as a shield, letting Ed safely advance and start up his offense.

Light & Medium Psycho Flicker (Hold Version) (↓↘→ + Hold Light Kick or Medium Kick)
The distance that opponents are pulled in to Ed on block is now reduced, which means when blocked at a certain distance, opponents will be outside of Ed's throw range. While Ed still has some strong poke and pressure tools after this attack is blocked, he no longer has an easy way of creating a favorable situation for him with his throw pressure, forcing Ed to be more creative with their game plan. For the defender, this also lowers the disadvantage they face from blocking this move, making this attack easier to deal with.

M. Bison.concept:
With M. Bison, we looked at improving his special moves that didn't see much use, as well as adjusting the range on his standing heavy punch, one of his key poking attacks at mid-range.

Bison receives an increased advantage on hit, and can now link to his far-reaching standing light punch, improving its utility as a high-reward poke that's capable of going into combos.

Overdrive Backfist Combo (Psycho Mine) (↓↙←+Two Punches)
You now have a lot more time to follow-up with an attack after this move hits, giving you options such as Heavy Backfist Combo or Overdrive Double Knee Press even when in the middle of the screen. When a Psycho Mine is embedded, you can now choose between those options or something like Overdrive Psycho Crusher Attack, which can give you even bigger returns due to the Psycho Mine detonation, so players can choose between going for high damage or more follow-up options.

Overdrive Shadow Rise (Charge ↓, then ↑+Two Kicks)
We increased the speed at which the move reaches the opponent and extended the window for transitioning into follow-up attacks, improving its effectiveness as a surprise attack.

Terry.concept:
Terry is a character with great damage and corner carry, and he as such he expects to get a lot out of his cancel-able medium and heavy attacks. His medium pokes in standing and crouching medium punch as well as crouching medium kick have different strengths, but standing medium punch had comparatively good reach and advantage, making it too good as both a counter-poke and for whiff punishing. That lead to it being so useful that it outshone his other pokes, so we've given it more recovery on whiff to tone it down.

Other than that, we shored up his special moves that were less useful by adjusting their parameters.

Standing Medium Punch
We extended the hurtbox forward while it is whiffing. This is a move that leads into target combos and can cancel into Drive Rush, so we've emphasized its use as a poke with good range and tried to limited its use as a counter-poke.

It's now more dangerous when it whiffs, so you'll need to think about when you used it at close and mid-ranges.

Round Wave (↓↘→+Heavy Punch)
The standby block timing has become 5 frames faster, so now it should be more difficult for opponents to escape when canceling into this from a standing or crouching medium punch that connects at the tip. This in turn should strengthen Terry's low attacks and pressure.

Overdrive Quick Burn (↓↙←+Two Punches)
The last hit has higher damage and also knocks the opponent back less far, giving you a better advantage. It's already useful as a combo into Super Art 2 and as a surprise overhead on the second attack, so now it's also a pathway into better damage and advantage when comboing from light attacks.

Mai.concept:
Mai has changes to her frequently used normal and special moves. These were a cause of her extremely lopsided choice of pokes and Super Arts, so these have been toned down. This should give more breathing room for the rest of her toolkit.

The main change to her pokes was making her standing medium punch more risky, as well as her limiting the invincibility on her Super Art 1 to make it less of a rock-solid tool to be used in combos as well as a counter attack. In exchange, we've improved her crouching heavy punch and added new properties to her Super Art 2. This should give her new opportunities to use her super gauge without making it feel like her tools have become too limited.

Although in general a few of her moves have decreased in strength, Overdrive Ryuuenbu has had its properties completely changed, so please try adding this to your repertoire and explore its new uses.

Crouching Heavy Punch
The standby block timing and distance moved forward have increased, which should make it so even if the first hit whiffs, the second hit should connect when used at the correct distance. The risk/reward has also improved through the changes in the pushback on hit and block. Altogether this move should now be much more useful at mid-ranges when covering your opponent getting up, or as a read for a whiff punish.

Jumping Medium Punch
This now knocks the opponent back horizontally on hit, which should make it easier to follow into Musasabi no Mai when hitting air-to-air, as well as make it possible to combo Overdrive Hissatsu Shinobi Bachi > jumping medium punch > Super Art 1 mid-screen. While this is detailed below, it is no longer possible to combo into Super Art 1 from Overdrive Ryuuenbu, so this now may be your main route for getting stocks from Super Art 1.

Normal Kachousen (regular or boosted) (↓↘→+Punch)
We've made the startup animation slightly more distinct so that it's easier to tell when this move is being used. The startup of this move was less pronounced than other projectiles, so now responding to the animation should be more in line with similar moves.

Overdrive Ryuuenbu (regular and boosted) (↓↙←+Two Punches)
It wasn't clear how this move and Overdrive Hissatsu Shinobi Bachi were supposed to differ, so we've made large adjustments here to remedy that. Extending your combos is now the role of Overdrive Hissatsu Shinobi Bachi, while Overdrive Ryuuenbu now has uses in catching overeager opponents.

Generally speaking, when you cancel into this from a medium attack you can combo on hit, while on guard you can frame trap your opponent. Once you plant the seed of doubt in them with this move, you can forgo canceling and go for more offense, force them to block a charged Kachousen, or use anything else in your repertoire.

Although this move was mostly used to combo into Super Arts midscreen, you are still able to continue your combos after it when used in the corner. This is especially true as the powered-up version now wall splats, making it an interesting new tool in both pressure and in combos.

Kagerou no Mai (Super Art 1) (regular and boosted) (↓↘→↓↘→+Punch)
The benefit this gave for turning over a bad situation was far greater than normal, and thus we believe it was being relied on far too much. Taking this into account, we've changed the invincibility of this move to only cover aerial moves, so it can no longer be used on wake up or as a counter attack.

This also means it can no longer be used as a counter attack against Drive Impact during burnout. You'll now need to manage your gauges differently now that you no longer have protection when you only have one bar of Super Art Gauge in burnout.

Air Chou Hissatsu Shinobi Bachi (Super Art 2) (regular or boosted) (↓↘→↓↘→+Kick during forward or neutral jump)
Most of the damage has now been concentrated in the last hit, and the move now does more damage on counter and Punish Counter, giving you more return successfully doing things like reading your opponent's projectile.

Elena.concept:
In this update, Elena has received some quality-of-life improvements aimed at addressing some of the finer issues in her toolkit. We've made her crouching medium kick easier to use, which is one of her primary tools in the neutral, and we've also reviewed the hitboxes of her special moves and added combo-only hitboxes where necessary. These changes reduce the difficulty of combos that previously required precise spacing or delayed timing to perform consistently.

Crouching Medium Kick
The frame disadvantage on block has been changed from -4F to -3F.
At close range, Elena often had difficulty reaching opponents who were backing away with sequences starting from Crouching Light Kick. As a result, she frequently relied on Crouching Medium Kick, despite the risk associated with a move that was -4F on block.
This adjustment is intended to reduce that risk and make the move easier to use in these situations.

Crouching Heavy Punch
The hit reaction of the second hit has been changed to a blow-away knockdown.
Elena can now convert into air combos in specific situations, such as when the move is used as an early air-to-air attack against an opponent's jump and only the second hit connects, or after landing a Drive Impact in the corner.

OD Spinning Scythe (↓↙← + Two Kicks)
A special hitbox that only connects during combos has been added to the first hit.
Previously, when used in certain sequences, the first hit could occasionally whiff despite appearing as though it should connect. This adjustment improves consistency and lowers the execution difficulty of those combos.

Super Art 2: Revival Dance (↓↘→↓↘→ + Punch) / Super Art 3: Song of the Grasslands (↓↙←↓↙← + Kick)
When either of these Super Arts was canceled from OD Rhino Horn, Elena would often pass underneath airborne opponents.
To address this issue, the pushbox has been expanded upward only when these Super Arts are canceled from OD Rhino Horn, preventing Elena from going underneath airborne opponents and improving combo reliability.

Sagat.concept:
Sagat's mid and close-range poking tools were providing too much value, so we've made adjustments to better balance the risk-reward of his key neutral tools. These adjustments include adding initial scaling to his crouching medium punch, and adjusting the risk-reward balance for standing medium kick by delaying the startup of its standby block hitbox and expanding its hurtbox.

At the same time, we've looked at expanding the number of tools to use in his neutral game by increasing the knockback on his standing light kick and increased the launch time on his Overdrive Tiger Nexus (↓↙← + Two Kicks) > Overdrive Tiger Greed on hit, etc.

Standing Light Kick
The advantage on this attack has changed from -1 frame to 0 frames. When used as a counter-poke, generally players could only follow-up with Heavy Tiger Uppercut, which was difficult to execute and had a high risk if it didn't work, but now it can lead to combos with Medium Tiger Nexus, or with Overdrive Tiger Knee when hitting with the tip of the kick.

Crouching Medium Punch
This attack served as Sagat's main zoning tool thanks to its ease of use and cancelable properties, but the return it got from neutral was proving to be too much, so we added initial scaling of 15% to the attack, which will lower combo damage when canceling the attack into Drive Rush into a combo.

We've also increased the damage on Tiger Slash and Tiger Rise. By adding initial scaling to crouching punch, the damage on crouching medium punch when used to start combos decreases, but when used in other parts of a combo, the damage is increased.

Overdrive Tiger Nexus (↓↙← + Two Kicks) > Overdrive Mighty Tiger (→ + Medium Kick) / Overdrive Greedy Tiger (→ + Heavy Kick)
Overdrive Tiger Nova has been the overwhelmingly preferred follow-up due to its utility and effectiveness as a combo tool, and players had few reasons to use Overdrive Mighty Tiger or Greedy Tiger. With this round of adjustments, we looked to give Sagat's other two options distinct advantages and increase their overall payoff.

The hit effect on counter hit Overdrive Mighty Tiger has been changed to a ground bound, allowing for follow-ups like Medium Tiger Uppercut. On block, the attack now leaves Sagat at -3 frames. With Overdrive Greedy Tiger, we've increased the launch duration on hit, so available combo routes have changed.

C. Viper.concept:
We've adjusted both Viper's normal and special moves, along with changes aimed at reducing difficulty and unintended inputs related to her High Jump cancel mechanics. We've improved her inputs to make execution errors less likely, allowing players to take more advantage of her versatile movement options.

High Jump (press ↑ immediately after ↓)
When performing a High Jump after canceling from normal attacks or Seismic Hammer, which can only be canceled into a High Jump, it is no longer necessary to return your input to neutral before entering the upward input for the High Jump. This reduces the amount of required input execution and makes unintended special moves less likely to occur. Now that crouching medium kick can now be High Jump Canceled directly from a down input without passing through neutral, has become significantly easier to cancel into High Jump consistently.

Standing Medium Kick
The hitstun on this move has been increased, allowing Focus Force to connect after a High Jump cancel. Now from situations such as counter hit crouching heavy punch > Heavy Thunder Dash (Feint) > standing medium kick, Viper can score knockdowns outside of spending Drive gauge with just a High Jump cancel. Viper can now also perform counter hit standing medium kick into Seismic Hammer via High Jump cancel if your input is fast enough, giving players more time to hit confirm before committing to the follow-up.

Overdrive Seismic Hammer (→↓↘ + Two Punches)
The frame data has been adjusted to make the move more useful outside of combo extensions, and its follow-up options have been expanded. The disadvantage on block is -6 frames, making it easier to use as a zoning tool, and you can also gain an advantage from High Jump cancel > Heavy Thunder Dash (Feint).

The combo count values on hit have also been adjusted, allowing you to combo with crouching heavy kick. While the attack may not connect if Overdrive Seismic Hammer connects at maximum range, Viper now has more follow-up attacks to utilize without requiring a High Jump cancel, making it more rewarding when using the attack in neutral.

Focus Force (normal and overdrive) (↓↙←+Kick or Two Kicks)
We observed cases where among Viper's various special move inputs, unintentional inputs would often occur especially when canceling a normal move or high jump canceling into a feinted Thunder Dash. Using feints in her pressure is one of Viper's most important features, so we felt that the amount of unintentional inputs were hampering the ability to enjoy her uniqueness as a character.

While this is a very specific fix, if you complete the input for Focus Force while holding any punch button, it now will not come out regardless of the version. Canceling from a normal or high jump into Thunder Dash and feinting requires a punch input, so this change should make unintended inputs come out much less frequently.

Although canceling into Focus Force from medium or heavy punch will now require you to let go of the punch button making it slightly more difficult, this should altogether be a positive change for controlling Viper.

Alex.concept:
Adjustments for Alex primarily focus on improving the usability of his normal and unique attacks, as well as improving his Prowler Stance (↓ + Two Punches) follow-ups, which is his defining character mechanic.

We've made it easier for Alex to apply pressure when playing the ground game by adjusting the frame advantage on hit for Standing Medium Punch and giving him a bigger advantage on block for Oblique Stomp (← + Medium Kick).

These options, combined with his Power Bomb (→↘↓↙← + Punch) and various Prowler Stance attacks will further strengthen Alex's specialized play style that focuses on keeping opponents on their toes and preventing them from narrowing down his options.

In addition, Flying Cross Chop (↓ + Heavy Punch during a forward jump) was being primarily used as a tool to escape from the corner, but it can now be canceled into from jumping medium punch, which will significantly improve the reward he gets from air-to-air encounters. This adjustment also opens up new combo routes from standing combo starters.

Normal Attacks/Unique Attacks
The frame advantage on hit for standing medium punch has changed from +3 frames to +4 frames. As a result, what you can follow up with on counter hit or Punish Counter is different, allowing Alex to apply more pressure with his strikes from close and mid-range. To complement the changes to his Prowler Stance-related attacks, crouching heavy kick can now transition into Prowler Stance as well. This gives Alex another offensive threat after scoring a knockdown, and will require players to change their thinking on existing pressure situations.

Heavy Power Bomb
The grab range of the attack has been slightly extended forward. Previously, after using approaches such as light attacks canceled into Drive Rush, this move would often whiff on the opponent due to being out of range. This adjustment is intended to increase the pressure and threat level of his throw game.

Dangerous Armbar
(↓ + Light Punch + Light Kick during Prowler Stance)
Projectile invincibility has been added from frame 3 until the active frames of the attack end. Before, if Alex entered Prowler Stance at a distance, Alex's primary anti-projectile options were Tactical Hop and Air Stampede. With this adjustment, Alex has another way to bypass projectiles, making him a much bigger threat at long range by forcing his opponents to keep tabs on yet another option in his arsenal.

Ingrid.concept:

Standing Medium Kick
By increasing this move's knockback time on hit, we made it possible to follow up a Punish Counter or Drive Rush version with Heavy Sun Rise. Whether it's a counterattack or counter poke, we wanted to expand the number of situations open to high-damage combos.

Heavy Sun Shot (↓↘→+ Heavy Punch) and Overdrive Sun Shot (↓↘→+ Two Punches)
By increasing the blowback caused by this move when it connects with an airborne opponent, Ingrid can now follow-up with attacks like Sun Flare or Drive Rush combos. The adjusted knockback time of the heavy version should have no effect on Ingrid's previous set-ups. We wanted the Overdrive version to have the same follow-up difficulty as the ordinary version would have on an mid-air hit, hence the combo count adjustments.
